title: Referee
summary: You agree to referee a Sunday league charity match. Your old school mate is playing, and in the seventieth minute he does something you have to send him off for. A season on, the charity match again.

ends.title: The red
ends.text: You refereed a charity match and sent off your oldest mate. He framed the red card. It hangs in his downstairs toilet.

ends.title: The whistle
ends.text: You refereed a charity match and let your mate off. Both teams still call you the worst ref they've ever had, fondly.

beats.title: Seventy minutes

event.title: Seventy minutes
event.speaker: pal
setup: Sunday league, a charity match for the air ambulance, and you're the ref. {pal.name} is centre half for the Red Lion. Seventy minutes in he goes through their striker like a lorry, and then looks at you and grins.

say: "Go on, then. You haven't got the guts."

red.text: The whole pitch goes up. He walks off slowly, applauding you, and asks for the card. You give it to him. He's going to frame it.

yellow.text: The other team surrounds you. You book three of them for that. It's the longest charity match in history.

nothing.text: Their striker's mum comes on to the pitch to tell you what she thinks. She's right.

beats.hint: A Sunday morning with a whistle

beats.title: The rematch

event.title: The rematch
event.speaker: pal
setup: A season on. {pal.short}: "Charity match again. They've asked for you to ref. I've asked for a different ref. They said no."

outcomes.text: He behaves for sixty-nine minutes. In the seventieth he looks at you, very deliberately, and doesn't tackle anyone. The whole pitch claps.
They give you a new whistle with "PLEASE" engraved on it.
He sends a photo from the match: the framed red card, held up at the side of the pitch.
"They said you were the worst ref they'd ever had," he says. "They meant it nicely."

beats.hint: A season on, the charity match again
